source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains Bethany, Simon’s descriptor, the woman’s anonymity, costly nard, broken vessel, and anointing of Jesus’ head.
key_decisions.before: While Jesus was in Bethany at the house of Simon the leper, reclining at the table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume made from pure nard. She broke the jar and poured the perfume over his head.
key_decisions.after: While Jesus was in Bethany, reclining at the table in the house of Simon the leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume made from pure nard. She broke the jar and poured the perfume over his head.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And while he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he was reclining at table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of costly ointment of pure nard. Breaking the jar, she poured it over his head.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the exact threshold, proposed recipients, and the intensity of their rebuke toward the woman.
key_decisions.before: It could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.
key_decisions.after: It could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her harshly.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” And they were scolding her.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps both defense questions and kalon’s aesthetic and moral force without reducing the act to utility.
key_decisions.before: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a beautiful work for me.
key_decisions.after: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why are you causing her trouble? She has done a beautiful work for me.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a beautiful work for me.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves continuing opportunity to aid the poor and the immediate contrast of Jesus’ limited presence.
key_decisions.before: You always have the poor with you, and whenever you want, you can do good for them. But you do not always have me.
key_decisions.after: You always have the poor with you, and whenever you want, you can do good for them. But you will not always have me.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish you are able to do good for them; but you do not always have me.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps her action within her capacity and Jesus’ interpretation of it as advance burial preparation.
key_decisions.before: She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for burial.
key_decisions.after: She did what she could. She anointed my body beforehand for burial.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: She has done what she could; she has anointed my body beforehand for burial.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains worldwide proclamation and the promise that her deed and memory accompany it.
key_decisions.before: Truly I tell you, wherever the good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
key_decisions.after: Truly I tell you, wherever the good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Truly I say to you, wherever the good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the nested speech, my guest room, and meal with the disciples.
key_decisions.before: Wherever he enters, say to the owner of the house, ‘The Teacher asks, Where is my guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’
key_decisions.after: Wherever he enters, say to the owner of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the intimate shared meal and repetition that the betrayer is among them.
key_decisions.before: While they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you will hand me over—one who is eating with me.”
key_decisions.after: As they reclined at the table and ate, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you will hand me over—one who is eating with me.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I say to you, one of you will hand me over, one who is eating with me.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains membership in the Twelve and shared-bowl image without identifying the person by name here.
key_decisions.before: He said to them, “It is one of the twelve, one who dips into the bowl with me.
key_decisions.after: He said to them, “It is one of the Twelve—one who dips bread into the bowl with me.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “It is one of the twelve, one who dips with me into the bowl.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves scriptural direction, human agency, woe, and the severe final judgment without resolving their relation.
key_decisions.before: The Son of Man goes just as it is written about him, but woe to the person through whom the Son of Man is handed over. It would have been better for that person not to have been born.”
key_decisions.after: The Son of Man goes just as it is written about him, but woe to that person through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been better for that person if he had not been born.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For the Son of Man goes just as it is written of him, but woe to that one through whom the Son of Man is handed over. It would have been good for that one if he had not been born.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the take–bless–break–give sequence and compact identification without adding sacramental instructions.
key_decisions.before: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, gave it to them, and said, “Take it. This is my body.”
key_decisions.after: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing, broke it, gave it to them, and said, “Take it; this is my body.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And while they were eating, taking bread, blessing it, he broke it and gave it to them and said, “Take; this is my body.”

key_decisions.rationale: Follows the pinned blood of the covenant without adding new and retains the many and pouring-out language.
key_decisions.before: He said to them, “This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
key_decisions.after: He said to them, “This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the emphatic abstention, fruit-of-the-vine image, future day, and kingdom horizon.
key_decisions.before: Truly I tell you, I will certainly not drink again from the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
key_decisions.after: Truly I tell you, I will certainly not drink again from the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in God’s kingdom.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Truly I say to you, I will no longer drink from the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the comprehensive prediction and quotation’s divine first person, shepherd, and scattered sheep.
key_decisions.before: Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, because it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
key_decisions.after: Jesus said to them, “All of you will fall away, because it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

key_decisions.rationale: Retains both temporal intensifiers and the exact two crowings and three denials.
key_decisions.before: Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today—this very night—before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today—this very night—before a rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to him, “Truly I say to you, today, this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Peter’s excessive insistence, willingness to die, emphatic denial, and the others’ identical claim.
key_decisions.before: But Peter insisted emphatically, “Even if I have to die with you, I will never deny you.” And all the others said the same.
key_decisions.after: But Peter kept insisting, “Even if I must die with you, I will never deny you.” And all the others said the same.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But he was saying emphatically, “If I must die with you, I will certainly not deny you.” And all were saying the same.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the three named companions and the intensity of Jesus’ distress.
key_decisions.before: He took Peter, James, and John with him and began to be deeply distressed and troubled.
key_decisions.after: He took Peter, James, and John with him and began to be overwhelmed and deeply troubled.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he took Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be greatly distressed and troubled.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves soul, mortal sorrow, and repeated staying with vigilance.
key_decisions.before: He said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Stay here and watch.”
key_decisions.after: He said to them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and stay awake.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, even to death. Remain here and watch.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps bodily collapse, conditional possibility, and hour as the image of impending suffering.
key_decisions.before: Going a little farther, he fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.
key_decisions.after: Going a little farther, he fell to the ground and prayed that, if possible, the hour might pass from him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And going forward a little, he fell on the ground and was praying that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains both forms of address, divine ability, genuine desire, cup image, and yielded will.
key_decisions.before: He said, “Abba, Father, everything is possible for you. Take this cup away from me. Yet not what I want, but what you want.”
key_decisions.after: He said, “Abba, Father, everything is possible for you. Take this cup away from me. Yet not what I want, but what you want.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he was saying, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Remove this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains both imperatives, the testing danger, and spirit–flesh contrast without explaining it doctrinally.
key_decisions.before: Watch and pray so that you do not enter into testing. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
key_decisions.after: Stay awake and pray so that you do not enter into testing. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Watch and pray, so that you may not come into testing. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the difficult apechei as a concise finality, the arrived hour, and repeated handing-over language.
key_decisions.before: He came a third time and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough. The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
key_decisions.after: He came a third time and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he came the third time and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Judas unnamed in the role label, the kiss as signal, and two commands including guarded removal.
key_decisions.before: The one handing Jesus over had given them a signal: “The one I kiss is the man. Arrest him and lead him away under guard.”
key_decisions.after: The one handing Jesus over had given them a signal: “The one I kiss is the man. Arrest him and lead him away securely.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now the one handing him over had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is he; seize him and lead him away securely.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the two immediacy markers, address, and identifying kiss.
key_decisions.before: As soon as Judas arrived, he went up to Jesus and said, “Rabbi!” and kissed him.
key_decisions.after: As soon as Judas arrived, he went straight to Jesus, said, “Rabbi!” and kissed him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And coming immediately, he went up to him and said, “Rabbi!” And he kissed him.

key_decisions.rationale: Leaves the assailant unnamed, retains slave status, and reports the actual injury without harmonizing later accounts.
key_decisions.before: One of those standing nearby drew a sword, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
key_decisions.after: One of those standing nearby drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But one of those standing by drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the contrast between public teaching and nighttime arrest and the terse fulfillment statement.
key_decisions.before: Day after day I was with you teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But let the Scriptures be fulfilled.”
key_decisions.after: Day after day I was with you, teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But let the Scriptures be fulfilled.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Day by day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me. But let the scriptures be fulfilled.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the follower’s anonymity, vulnerable dress, nakedness, and seizure while continuing the sentence.
key_decisions.before: A young man was following him wearing only a linen cloth over his naked body. They seized him,
key_decisions.after: A young man was following him, wearing nothing but a linen cloth over his naked body. They seized him,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And a certain young man was following him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body, and they seized him;

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the startling naked escape without identifying or allegorizing him.
key_decisions.before: but he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.
key_decisions.after: but he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: but leaving the linen cloth, he fled naked.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains first-person claim, made-by-hands contrast, and three-day construction without validating the testimony.
key_decisions.before: saying, “We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple made by hands, and in three days I will build another not made by hands.’”
key_decisions.after: “We heard him say, ‘I will tear down this temple made by hands and in three days build another not made by hands.’”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: “We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made with hands.’”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Jesus’ silence and the two-part identity question with reverential divine title.
key_decisions.before: But Jesus remained silent and gave no answer. Again the high priest asked him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
key_decisions.after: But Jesus remained silent and gave no answer. Again the high priest questioned him: “Are you the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But he was silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him and said to him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the direct affirmation and combined enthronement and cloud-coming imagery.
key_decisions.before: Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said, “I am; and you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

key_decisions.rationale: Names the humiliating violence concretely and keeps attendants’ final action without softening it.
key_decisions.before: Some began to spit on him. They covered his face, struck him, and said, “Prophesy!” The attendants also received him with blows.
key_decisions.after: Some began to spit on him, cover his face, strike him with their fists, and say, “Prophesy!” The attendants also struck him with slaps.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And some began to spit on him and to cover his face and strike him, saying to him, “Prophesy!” And the attendants received him with blows.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the twofold denial of comprehension, movement, and first rooster crow present in the pinned text.
key_decisions.before: But he denied it: “I neither know nor understand what you are talking about.” He went out into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.
key_decisions.after: But Peter denied it: “I neither know nor understand what you are talking about.” He went out into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But he denied it, saying, “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” And he went out into the forecourt, and the rooster crowed.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the second denial, repeated accusers, Galilean identity, and speech evidence present in the pinned verse.
key_decisions.before: But he denied it again. After a little while, the people standing there said to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, because you are a Galilean.”
key_decisions.after: But Peter denied it again. After a little while, those standing there said to him again, “Surely you are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech sounds like it.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But again he was denying it. And after a little while, again those standing by were saying to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you are also a Galilean.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves both cursing and oath-taking and Peter’s distancing phrase this man.
key_decisions.before: But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man you are talking about!”
key_decisions.after: But he began to call down curses and swear, “I do not know this man you are talking about!”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But he began to curse and to swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps second crow, exact recalled prediction, and the uncertain final verb rendered as collapse into weeping.
key_decisions.before: Immediately the rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” And he broke down and wept.
key_decisions.after: Immediately a rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: “Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” And he broke down and wept.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And immediately the rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word, how Jesus had said to him, “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” And breaking down, he wept.
